subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact Private Mode contract should OpenClaw guarantee across context reads, transcript/session storage, memory, plugin artifacts, channel history, logs, and dashboard UI?
rationale: The requested behavior is a privacy/security product boundary that spans several owners, and source inspection shows no current single mode or field that downstream paths can safely enforce.

options.title: Design a shared core contract
options.body: Add a single private-session mode with explicit no-context/no-persist semantics and require every storage, memory, plugin, channel, and UI path to respect it.

options.title: Narrow to context suppression
options.body: Ship only a clearly named context-suppression mode if maintainers want a smaller feature that does not promise no durable history or memory writes.

options.title: Defer and document mitigations
options.body: Keep the issue open while documenting current partial mitigations such as disabling context injection and memory features without claiming private sessions.

recommendation.title: Design a shared core contract
recommendation.body: Add a single private-session mode with explicit no-context/no-persist semantics and require every storage, memory, plugin, channel, and UI path to respect it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is product/security-contract heavy and prior review already treated #7403 as the canonical private-mode tracker.
